title: The address space that ran out

probes.question: True or false: IPv4 address exhaustion was one of the reasons IPv6 was developed.

image.alt: Colorful orange, blue and green network cables spilling from ceiling trays above server cabinets in a computer lab.

panels.text: When the internet was an experiment, 32-bit addresses were chosen. That gives about 4.3 billion of them. Running out was not an early concern.
The experiment escaped. Users multiplied, and depletion had been anticipated since the late 1980s.
On 31 January 2011, the last two unreserved top-level blocks of IPv4 addresses were allocated.
The successor is IPv6, with 128-bit addresses: about 340 undecillion of them. The two protocols coexist.
